question.text: Conquistadors from this European nation conquered the Incas. This empire established colonies in all of Central America and most of South America.
question.clue: The sixteenth century Dutch Revolt was against this country.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about Muslim Spain.
swap.text: This long series of wars between Christians and Muslims for control of Iberia included El Cid. It ended in 1492 when Ferdinand and Isabella accepted Grenada's surrender.
swap.clue: It is often held to have begun at Covadonga and was completed with expulsion of the Nasrids under Boabdil and the destruction of al-Andalus.

question.leadin: Answer the following about Portuguese colonial history.
question.text: Later modified by the Treaty of Zaragoza to include the Moluccas, this treaty set up a line of demarcation dividing the world between Spain and Portugal.
question.clue: This treaty established a line 370 leagues west of the Cape Verde Islands, which was later extended through both poles by the Treaty of Zaragoza.

swap.leadin: This fleet attempted to meet with the troops of the Duke of Parma but, while waiting at Gravelines, was attacked by the British navy and was forced to go north.
swap.text: Identify this fleet that King Philip II of Spain sent to conquer England in 1588.
swap.answerHtml: the Spanish Armada [accept Grande y Felicisima Armada or Armada Invencible]
swap.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

question.text: The right wing was controlled by this Kingdom. Henri IV ["the fourth"] of France was originally king of this polity, and it is the last polity controlled by the Basque community.
question.answerHtml: The Kingdom of Navarre [nah-VAHR] [prompt on Kingdom of Pamplona]
question.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

swap.text: This Catholic king of Spain and successor of Charles V sought the aid of Pope Sixtus V for an invasion of England with the Armada.
swap.clue: This man's attempts to force people to abandon their style of clothing led to the second revolt of the Moriscos.

question.leadin: This man gained nationwide prestige after he crushed the Asturias miners' strike of 1934.
question.text: Name this man, who sent the Blue Division to fight for Nazi Germany on the Eastern Front during World War II. This dictator ruled his country under the title El Caudillo and came to prominence for his services in the Rif War.
question.clue: This leader unified the Carlist and the Falange parties.

swap.text: The Sicilian Vespers happened concurrently with a crusade named after this region. A ruler of this Spanish region issued the Alhambra Decree and married Germaine de Foix.
swap.clue: This polity conquered Sicily in the wake of the Sicilian Vespers Uprising in 1282 during the reign of its "Great" king, Peter III.

question.leadin: During his period of imprisonment this party derisively nicknamed his founder "the Absent One," or el Ausente.
question.text: Name this spectrum of movements and political parties founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera, and named for an ancient military formation.
question.answerHtml: Falange [or Falange Espanola (es-PAN-yola) de la JONS; or FE de las JONS; accept word forms, such as Falangists]
question.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

swap.leadin: This monarch's forces defeated Joanna la Beltraneja in a war of succession, allowing her to inherit the throne from Henry IV.
swap.text: Name this queen who presided over the end of the Reconquista when Boabdil surrendered to her.
swap.answerHtml: Isabella I of Castile [or Isabella of Castile; prompt on "Isabella"]
swap.clue: She was succeeded by her daughter, Joanna the Mad, who began Hapsburg control of Spain by marrying Philip the Handsome.

question.leadin: This man's most important work centers on the examination of conscience.
question.text: Name this man who wrote a work that details an ideal retreat, which is laid out in four weeks, each of which details a segment of the life of Christ, The Spiritual Exercises.
question.answerHtml: Saint Ignatius of Loyola [prompt on Saint Ignatius; or Ignacio de Loyola]
question.clue: This mentor of Peter Faber and Diego Lainez expressed his belief that obedience was the pre-eminent virtue in his "Letter on Obedience."

swap.text: The first of the Spanish Bourbons was this grandson of Louis XIV. His accession in 1700 prompted the War of Spanish Succession, though he would stay in power until his death in 1746.
swap.clue: This king's opponents claimed that his reign was a violation of the Hague Partition Treaties.

question.leadin: John II offered people affected by this law asylum before deporting many to Sao Tome. but his son Manuel I was pressured into replicating the edict 5 years later.
question.text: Name this law, passed under the pretense of protecting conversos from subversion, which led migrants to settle in Mizrahi communities in Morocco and Algeria.
question.clue: The most famous such incident took place in Spain in 1492 through a decree named for this Muslim fort in Andalusia, one of the final holdouts to Ferdinand and Isabella.

swap.text: The Alhambra Decree, which expelled the Jews from Spain, was advocated by this Dominican Grand Inquisitor under Ferdinand and Isabella.
swap.clue: The co-rulers were also ardent supporters of the Inquisition, appointing this "hammer of heretics" as the brutal Grand Inquisitor.

question.text: Philip II's son, Philip III, expelled these people from Spain in 1609. These people were descendants of Muslims who had converted to Catholicism, and they rose up in revolt during the Rebellion of the Alpujarras.
question.clue: This silk trade-controlling group created the maritime Republic of Sale (SAL-ay), and unsuccessfully sought aid from the Huguenot stronghold of Bearn.

swap.text: This was the only city to remain in rebellion after the execution of Maldonado, Bravo, and Padilla. Padilla's wife, Maria Pacheco, led this city's defense for six more months until negotiating a peaceful surrender.
swap.clue: The third council in this city confirmed Reccared's decision to convert from Arianism to Catholicism.

question.leadin: The GAL, or Antiterrorist Liberation Groups, targeted this organization in the Monbar Hotel attack.
question.text: The newspaper The World exposed a PSOE leader's involvement in death squads targeting what organization? This organization's symbol was an axe with a snake around it, and it had the motto "Keep up in both."
question.answerHtml: ETA [or Euskadi Ta Askatasuna or Basque Homeland and Liberty or Basque Country and Freedom; prompt on Basque separatists]
question.clue: Members of this organization were prosecuted in the Burgos trials.

swap.text: The Reapers's War established a short-lived republic in this northeastern region of Spain, which has its own Romance dialect and distinct culture.
swap.clue: That one saw the loss of the Rousillon and Cerdagne, which were northern portions of this region.

question.leadin: This polity produced antipope Benedict XIII, who was backed its King Alfonso V the Magnanimous against Pope Martin V and the Sforzas. FTPE.
question.text: Identify this kingdom which under Alfonso incorporated Naples and Valencia, whose most revered King may have been John the Great, who faced a civil war following the birth of his son Charles of Viana that eventually forced him to relinquish Rousillon to Louis XI, and who would later become the grandfather of Joana the Mad.
question.clue: Pope Martin IV ("the fourth") ordered a crusade against this kingdom after its ruler Peter III ("the third") accepted a request to invade Sicily in response to the Sicilian Vespers.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Umayyad conquest of Hispania.
swap.text: This Umayyad commander captured Toledo after defeating the Visigothic king Roderic at the Battle of Guadalete in 711 CE. To honor this man, the Umayyads renamed a geographical feature on the Iberian Peninsula that had previously been known as Mons Calpe.
swap.answerHtml: Tariq [or Tariq ibn Ziyad; accept Jabal Tariq; reject “Gibraltar”] {The word “Gibraltar” is a corruption of “Jabal Tariq”, which means “Tariq’s mountain” in Arabic.}
